answer.rationale: Write path latency spike confined to primary region after recent release during peak settlement load suggests localized degradation. memory_b2 demonstrates regional failover's proven ability to restore latency within minutes during similar degradation patterns. Verifying memory_b1 to confirm rollback safety as secondary option if failover does not resolve. Failover chosen over rollback because: (1) release was stable enough to deploy, (2) degradation is regional not systemic, (3) peak settlement traffic makes rollback riskier than traffic shift, (4) failover preserves all writes while testing hypothesis, (5) if failover succeeds, we keep the release; if it fails, rollback remains available next window. Memory_b2 shows the exact recovery pattern we need. This is standard_experiment scale—full regional traffic shift but bounded to one region.
